National Conference on Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) Concludes in Mumbai with Focus on Strengthening Welfare and Skilling Ecosystem for Construction Workers
articles.full_content:
Secretary (Labour & Employment) Calls for Greater Synergy and Cross-Learning Between Centre and States to Strengthen BOCW Welfare Delivery States and UTs Showcase Initiatives on Skilling, Digital Labour Chowks and Worker Facilitation at BOCW Conference
The two-day National Conference on Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW), organised by the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, in collaboration with Government of Maharashtra, concluded today in Mumbai. The conference, held on September 11–12, 2026, brought together representatives of the Central Government, State/UT Governments, BOCW Welfare Boards and other stakeholders to deliberate on issues concerning the welfare, skilling, employment and social protection of construction workers. Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister of Labour and Employment and Youth Affairs and Sports, chaired Day 1 of the Conference, in presence of Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for Labour and Employment and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.
In his opening remarks on Day 2, the Secretary elaborated upon the current challenges and opportunities in the BOCW sector. Strengthening the skill ecosystem and placing dignity of labour at the centre of policy and programme design, he stressed, is critical to building a more responsive, inclusive and resilient labour ecosystem. He highlighted the need to address information and accessibility asymmetries in the labour market and strengthen mechanisms that facilitate better linkages between jobseekers and employers.
The Secretary underlined that the mobility of workers, both interstate and international, should be duly considered while designing social security and welfare schemes, and called for greater attention to occupational health, physical safety and other workplace concerns of construction workers.
Appreciating the best practices shared by States and UTs during the Conference, he encouraged greater exchange of experiences and more frequent virtual engagements between the Centre and States for sustained collaboration and mutual learning.
Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, delivered the opening remarks on Day 2 of the National Conference on BOCW, setting the tone for the day’s deliberations. https://t.co/rBEgP0gmEE
Looking ahead, the Secretary outlined key pathways for strengthening the BOCW welfare ecosystem, including consolidation of the diverse measures being undertaken and greater use of actuarial analysis to support sustainable welfare interventions.
The second day of the Conference commenced with a session on “Roles and Responsibilities of BOCW Welfare Boards in the light of the New Labour Codes.” The session featured presentations by various States/UTs, highlighting their initiatives and best practices aimed at strengthening welfare and service delivery for Building and Other Construction Workers.

NITI Aayog Member (Health) Prof. (Dr.) M. Srinivas Visits CCRAS-NIIMH, Hyderabad
articles.full_content:
Prof. (Dr.) M. Srinivas Calls for Global Standards and Greater Visibility of India’s Medical Heritage
Prof. (Dr.) M. Srinivas, Member (Health), NITI Aayog, Government of India, visited the CCRAS–National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage (NIIMH), Ministry of Ayush, Hyderabad. He was accompanied by Dr. Shobhit Kumar, OSD (Health), NITI Aayog, and Dr. Janvi Prajapati, Young Professional, NITI Aayog.
Dr. N. Srikanth, Deputy Director General, Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), New Delhi, welcomed Prof. Srinivas and briefed him on the institute’s initiatives, digital portals, repositories and historical research in traditional systems of medicine. He also emphasised the strategic role of NIIMH in documenting and preserving India’s rich medical heritage. Dr. Goli Penchala Prasad, Assistant Director In-charge, NIIMH, gave an overview of the institute’s activities, key milestones and achievements.
During the visit, Prof. Srinivas visited the museum, library and research divisions and interacted with officers and project staff. He also viewed a documentary on Agalya and the Rani Rudramadevi inscription, developed by the institute under the SAHI project.
Prof. (Dr.) M. Srinivas, in his address, commended the efforts of CCRAS–NIIMH in digitising rare manuscripts, maintaining historical scientific records and strengthening the preservation of India’s medical heritage through advanced information systems and research portals.
Prof. Srinivas called for adoption of international practices and standards for the preservation and maintenance of the museum. He also stressed the importance of introducing training courses, certificate courses and collaborative joint post-doctoral programmes to build capacity and develop skilled manpower for the preservation of India’s rich medical heritage.
Prof. Srinivas also suggested positioning NIIMH as a destination for educational tourism for students and professionals from medical and allied disciplines. He emphasised the need to enhance the institute’s visibility and global recognition.
He further recommended that NIIMH engage with regulatory bodies such as the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and the National Medical Commission (NMC) to connect with students and faculty. He also suggested developing mini-museums at IITs and other Institutions of National Importance to facilitate wider dissemination of India’s rich medical heritage.
Prof. Srinivas appreciated the efforts of the institute towards preserving India’s rich medical heritage and assured support for further strengthening its activities. In the visitors’ book, he described NIIMH as a “Temple” preserving India’s rich medical history and appreciated the dedication of its leadership and staff towards protecting and preserving the heritage for future generations.

NSKFDC Advances Socio-Economic Empowerment of Sanitation Workers through Concessional Finance and Skill Development
articles.full_content:
Corporation Sanctions and Disburses Rs. 3,365.93 Crore, Benefiting Over 6.10 Lakh Persons Since Inception Financial Assistance of up to Rs. 30 Lakh for Individuals and Rs 75 Lakh for Groups Available for Viable Self-Employment Activities
The National Safai Karamcharis Finance & Development Corporation (NSKFDC) , a wholly owned Government of India Undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, continues to promote sustainable livelihoods and socio-economic empowerment among Safai Karamcharis, waste pickers, manual scavengers and their dependents across the country.
Under its loan-based schemes, NSKFDC provides financial assistance at concessional rates of interest to eligible beneficiaries for undertaking viable self-employment and income-generating activities.
Financial assistance of up to Rs. 30 lakh is available to an individual beneficiary, while loans of up to Rs. 75 lakh may be extended to a group of beneficiaries. The applicable rate of interest ranges from 6% to 9% per annum, depending upon the nature and quantum of financial assistance. The repayment period ranges from three to ten years , subject to the amount of the loan and the provisions of the applicable scheme.
A rebate of 1% on the applicable rate of interest is provided to women beneficiaries. An additional rebate of 0.5% is available to beneficiaries for the timely repayment of instalments, in accordance with the applicable scheme guidelines.
The loan schemes are implemented through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) nominated by the respective State and Union Territory Governments, along with Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Public Sector Banks (PSBs).
In addition to financial assistance, NSKFDC implements non-loan-based programmes for the benefit of its target group. Financial assistance and grants are provided for organising awareness camps, workshops, skill-development initiatives and other capacity-building programmes.
These interventions seek to enhance employability, develop entrepreneurial capabilities and enable beneficiaries to access safer, dignified and sustainable livelihood opportunities.
Since its inception and up to 10 September 2026, NSKFDC has sanctioned and disbursed concessional loans amounting to Rs. 3,365.93 crore to its channelising agencies, covering 6,10,902 persons from its target group.
Through its financing schemes, skill-development programmes and capacity-building initiatives, NSKFDC remains committed to advancing social inclusion, economic independence and dignified livelihoods for sanitation workers and their dependents across the country.
Established on 24 January 1997 as a Not-For-Profit Company, NSKFDC has been operational since October 1997 as an apex corporation dedicated to the overall upliftment of its target communities. The Corporation implements a range of loan-based schemes and non-loan-based programmes to support self-employment, skill development, capacity-building and social empowerment.

CSIR-INTEGRATED SKILL INITIATIVE 2026
articles.full_content:
CSIR-Structural Engineering Research Centre (CSIR-SERC), Chennai organised a two-day workshop on Structural Engineering during 10-11 September 2026 at Sri Sivasubramaniya Nadar College of Engineering campus, near Chennai under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative. The workshop was organised for students across all academic years of Civil Engineering, providing them an opportunity to gain exposure to recent developments, emerging technologies and practical applications in structural engineering.
The CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative, a flagship national programme of the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), aims to create comprehensive skill-development opportunities by integrating education, practical skill development and real-world applications. The initiative is aligned with the vision of Skill India and the national goal of building an Atmanirbhar Bharat.
Dr. N. Anandavalli, Director, CSIR-SERC, Dr. R. Radha, Principal of the college and other dignitaries inaugurated the workshop.
Dr. Anandavalli, in her inaugural address highlighted the importance of complementing academic knowledge with practical skills. She emphasised on the need for students to understand real-world civil engineering challenges and apply their academic learning to develop practical and innovative solutions, thereby setting the tone for the two-day programme.
A team of scientists from CSIR-SERC delivered technical lectures and interacted with the students on contemporary topics covering various aspects of structural engineering, emerging technologies and innovation.
Dr. S. Parivallal, Scientist-G & Advisor, CSIR-SERC, gave a talk on Structural Health Monitoring of Civil Infrastructure. The session provided insights into the application of modern monitoring technologies for assessing the health condition and performance of structures.
The workshop provided the participants with valuable insights into civil and structural engineering, helping bridge the gap between academic knowledge and practical solutions through exposure to real-world engineering challenges, field applications and emerging technologies. The inclusion of the IPR session further broadened the scope of the programme by creating awareness about innovation, knowledge creation and intellectual property protection. The enthusiastic participation of the students, reflected in their active interaction and thoughtful questions, made the programme enriching and inspiring.
